issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree that completely partitions property by metes and bounds is a final decree even if it is later engrossed on stamp paper.
material_facts: The compromise schedules allocated specified properties to each group and the compromise decree described the properties allotted to them.
The parties took possession in accordance with the allocations, and no further inquiry or partition remained to be carried out.
A later decree on stamp paper reproduced the original decree without changing the allocations.
issues.conclusion: The original compromise decree was a final decree because it fully effected partition; later engrossment cured the stamping deficiency and the decree was effective from its original date.
issues.legal_principle: Order XX Rule 18 CPC permits a preliminary decree where further inquiry is required, but does not require one when the parties’ rights and the actual partition are fully determined. The Court approved Raghubir Sahu v. Ajodhya Sahu, AIR 1945 Pat 482, and agreed with Muzaffar Husain v. Sharafat Husain, AIR 1933 Oudh 562, and Thiruvengadathamiah v. Mungiah, (1912) 35 Mad 25. It distinguished Nachlappa Chettiar v. Subramaniam Chettiar, Gajanan Krishnaji Bapat v. Dattaji Raghobaji Meghe, Shanker Balwant Lokhande v. Chandrakant Shanker Lokhande, and M.L. Subbaraya Setty v. M.L. Nagappa Setty because those cases did not concern a compromise decree that had already effected partition by metes and bounds.

rule.if: partition_suit and compromise_allocated_specific_parcels and no_further_partition_inquiry and later_engrossed_on_stamp

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding was a suit to partition property or obtain separate possession of a share.
predicates.compromise_allocated_specific_parcels: The parties’ compromise specified the particular properties allotted to each share.
predicates.no_further_partition_inquiry: No further inquiry or act of partition remained necessary to identify the properties allotted to each share.
predicates.later_engrossed_on_stamp: The decree was later reproduced or engrossed on the required stamp paper.

issues.definition: When a partition proceeding ends in a compromise that allocates specific parcels and leaves no further partition inquiry, later engrossment on stamp paper makes the decree effective from its original date.

issues.legal_issue: A donee acquires title under a gift made after a complete partition decree allocates the gifted property to the donors, even if the decree is engrossed on stamp paper only later.
material_facts: The compromise decree allocated the house containing the disputed rooms to the donors and fully described the property allotted to them.
The donors executed and registered a gift of their interest in that property after the compromise decree but before its later engrossment on stamp paper.
The later engrossed decree reproduced the original allocation without alteration.
issues.conclusion: The donors could validly gift the allocated property before the later engrossment, and the donees acquired valid title under the gift.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XX Rule 18 CPC, a decree that fully determines and effects partition by metes and bounds may be final without a separate later determination of shares or parcels. The Court relied on Raghubir Sahu v. Ajodhya Sahu, AIR 1945 Pat 482, and agreed with Muzaffar Husain v. Sharafat Husain, AIR 1933 Oudh 562, and Thiruvengadathamiah v. Mungiah, (1912) 35 Mad 25. Because the later engrossment related back to the original decree, the donors’ allocation was effective when they made the gift.

rule.if: appeal_from_possession_and_rent_claims and partition_suit and property_allocated_to_grantors and gift_made_before_later_engrossment

predicates.appeal_from_possession_and_rent_claims: The proceeding is an appeal arising from claims for possession and rent based on an asserted title to property.
predicates.partition_suit: The asserted title arises from a suit to partition property or obtain separate possession of a share.
predicates.property_allocated_to_grantors: The partition decree allocated the gifted property to the persons who later made the gift.
predicates.gift_made_before_later_engrossment: The grantors made the gift after the original partition decree but before its later engrossment on stamp paper.

issues.definition: In an appeal arising from possession and rent claims, donees acquire valid title when the property was allocated to the grantors by a complete partition decree and the grantors made the gift before later engrossment.

issues.legal_issue: A grantor’s subsequent acquisition of title to property previously conveyed by a valid deed enures to the grantee under the doctrine of feeding the grant by estoppel.
material_facts: The donors had a pre-existing interest in the disputed property as members of a joint family, and their right to partition had been recognized in the original decree.
They executed and registered the gift before the later decree completed or confirmed their title to the allocated property.
The deed’s execution and registration were undisputed, and no invalidity in the deed was established.
The opposing occupants had no title to the disputed property and did not claim a bona fide purchase for value without notice.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming the donors had not acquired complete title when they made the gift, their subsequent acquisition of title enured to the donees and cured any defect in the donors’ title.
issues.legal_principle: The equitable doctrine of feeding the grant by estoppel applies when a grantor conveys an interest the grantor does not yet possess and later acquires title sufficient to satisfy the conveyance. The Court referred to Section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act as an illustration of the doctrine’s recognition in Indian law, but held that section did not directly apply because the gift was without consideration. It relied on Rajapakse v. Fernando, (1920) AC 892, and the rule stated in Tilakdhari Lal v. Khedan Lal. The doctrine does not apply where the deed itself is invalid or a third party has acquired title bona fide for value and without notice.

rule.if: title_challenge_in_possession_or_rent_proceeding and transfer_before_title_acquired and grantor_later_acquired_title and valid_transfer_deed and no_bona_fide_purchaser_without_notice

predicates.title_challenge_in_possession_or_rent_pr: The proceeding challenges a grantee’s title in a claim concerning possession or rent.
predicates.transfer_before_title_acquired: The grantor conveyed the property before acquiring complete title to it.
predicates.grantor_later_acquired_title: The grantor subsequently acquired title sufficient to satisfy the conveyance.
predicates.valid_transfer_deed: The transfer deed was validly executed and was not shown to be invalid.
predicates.no_bona_fide_purchaser_without_notice: No third party acquired title bona fide for value and without notice of the earlier transfer.

issues.definition: If a valid transfer precedes the grantor’s acquisition of title, and no protected bona fide purchaser intervenes, the later-acquired title enures to the grantee.
